newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian fuel minister says electricity revamp hard.
newsitem.headline: Russian fuel minister says electricity revamp hard.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said on Tuesday that the government had yet to come up with an adequate plan to restructure national electricity monopoly Unified Energy System, or UES.

"For the time being there exists no normal concept for the restructuring of the electrical energy sector -- nobody has a concept -- not the Economics Ministry, not even we," he told a news conference.

"Whatever wise decisions we might take, they would be impossible to incarnate with the shareholders of each energo whose shares are part of the RAO UES holding company," he said, adding that changes would have to be agreed with shareholders.
Analysts and the International Monetary Fund, as part of its $10 billion loan to Russia, have called on Moscow to create a wholesale electricity market and make power generators independent.

UES, or Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema, currently controls the generation, transmission and distribution of nearly all electricity. It owns minority stakes in most of the 72 regional "energo" utilities.
Rodionov said restructuring the natural gas monopoly, RAO Gazprom was simpler.
"The restructuring processes there are proceeding more simply -- sometimes even a board-level decision is enough there to take concrete steps," he said.
Rodionov, formerly the head of Gapzrom's distribution unit in St Petersburg, said that only the coal industry had seen real restructuring.

Analysts have said there has been little restructuring at Gazprom, the world's largest gas company, which controls nearly 100 percent of the production and distribution of gas in Russia. Some coal mines have been closed or reduced their activities.
